snippet.description:
Preparing for UPSC CSE 2027? Your CSAT strategy should depend on your current level of preparation, previous scores and areas of weakness.

In this video, Ma’am explains how UPSC aspirants can plan their CSAT preparation for 2027 based on three categories: beginners, borderline scorers and advanced aspirants. She discusses when to start, what to prioritise and how to prepare effectively instead of relying on shortcuts or leaving CSAT until the last few months.

Check CSAT Master Program 2027 by Himanshi Ma'am: https://www.levelupias.com/courses/upsc-cse-csat-foundation/

📌 What You’ll Learn in This Video:
- How recent changes in CSAT have affected question patterns, difficulty and time management
- Why you should prepare English, Reasoning and Quantitative Aptitude rather than depend on one section
- How to build a preparation strategy based on your current CSAT score
- The four essential steps: **Concepts, Practice Questions, PYQs and Mock Tests**
- Important CSAT Maths topics, including Number System, Averages, Percentages, Time and Work, and Time-Speed-Distance
- How to improve question selection through sectional tests, full-length mocks and test analysis
- When beginners, borderline scorers and advanced aspirants should begin their CSAT preparation for UPSC 2027

**The key takeaway:** CSAT preparation is not just about solving questions. It requires conceptual clarity, repeated practice, previous-year question analysis and the ability to manage time during the examination.

If you are a UPSC repeater or preparing for your first attempt in 2027, use this practical CSAT strategy to assess your current level and plan your next steps.

Watch till the end and share your CSAT preparation questions in the comments.

snippet.description:
What matters more in Sociology Optional answer writing: addressing the demand of the question or adding multiple thinkers?

In this video, AIR 22 Geetika Arora (UPSC CSE 2025) shares a key lesson she learnt from Nishat Sir: focus on what the question demands instead of feeling pressured to include four or five thinkers in every answer.

Her approach was simple: understand the question, address its demand, and use thinkers naturally wherever relevant.

For Sociology Optional aspirants, this is an important reminder that answer relevance matters more than unnecessary complexity.
